_purpose: Shared UAE/GCC facts every guide claim is checked against (the U check). Internal evidence only; never cited on the page. confidence: high = official/peer-reviewed or several agreeing sources; medium = consistent secondary sources; low = single or conflicting sources, needs local confirmation.

facts.fact: Dubai summer (Jun–Sep) average highs about 41–42 °C, average lows about 29–32 °C: nights do not cool down. Outdoor plants get no night-time relief.
facts.note: Third-party climate sites; NCM normals not retrieved. Check ncm.ae when possible.

facts.fact: Coastal UAE (Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah) January average lows about 14–16 °C. Cold damage to tropical plants is rare on the coast.

Inland and mountain UAE get much colder winter nights: Raknah (Al Ain) recorded -2 °C in Jan 2021, Jebel Jais -5.7 °C in Feb 2017; lows of 3–5 °C are reported most winters. Outdoor tropical plants in Al Ain, Liwa, desert villas and RAK mountains can get cold damage.

Elsewhere in the GCC, winter is colder than coastal UAE: Riyadh and Kuwait January lows about 7–10 °C with colder spells; Doha about 11–16 °C; Muscat mild. Advice about 'winter is no problem' must be limited to coastal UAE.
facts.note: Sources disagree; use ranges, not single numbers.

facts.fact: Homes and offices are air-conditioned most of the year (design target about 22–24 °C). Indoor humidity under AC is NOT reliably dry: a Sharjah workspace study measured average 60.7% RH at 21.6 °C. Some homes feel dry, others humid. Do not claim 'dry AC air' as a general UAE fact.
facts.note: Workspaces, not homes. No measured home study found.

facts.fact: Direct cold draughts from AC vents (split units, ceiling diffusers) are a common cause of leaf damage on indoor plants in UAE homes.
facts.note: Nursery experience; confirm with PlantsWorld staff.

facts.fact: UAE tap water is desalinated (mostly reverse osmosis / thermal), then remineralised with calcium and magnesium. Hardness is disputed and varies by emirate, source and building tank: one secondary source reports 150–250 mg/L as CaCO3 (hard), another 40–120 mg/L (soft). Do not call it 'hard' in general; tie flushing advice to visible salt crust or brown tips.
facts.note: No DEWA primary figure found. The earlier "often hard" wording was withdrawn on 31 Oct.

facts.fact: UAE sun is intense year-round; west- and south-facing glass in flats and villas gives strong afternoon heat and light. Many towers have tinted glazing, which reduces light indoors.
facts.note: General knowledge; confirm with staff experience.

facts.fact: Gardening season in the UAE is about October to April. May to September outdoor plants need shade and more frequent watering; most planting and repotting is done in the cooler months.
Rain is rare but can be heavy in short bursts (mostly Nov–Apr). Outdoor pots without drainage holes can flood.
